transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sophie (Redwood CSM), Daniel, Priya, Tom, Liam (Crestview)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Crestview is evaluating Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for production inference. Key concerns: isolation/data residency, predictable throughput for trading/analytics workloads, burst handling for end-of-day jobs, and security/SOC2. They are interested in a 1-week pilot/benchmark and want committed pricing and network diagrams.
Topics: Dedicated capacity sizing, burst strategy, autoscaling/burst, security/VPC peering, KMS/encryption, on-prem vs VPC tradeoffs, SLA expectations.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick intros?
[00:00:06] Daniel: Yep, Dan here, Head of Infra at Crestview. we run infra for their ml and trading apps.
[00:00:10] Priya: Hi, Priya, lead ML engineer, focusing on model serving and latency.
[00:00:13] Tom: Tom, CTO. short on time but wanted to join first 20 to hear high level.
[00:00:18] Liam: Liam security architect, i'll ask the weird firewall questions.
[00:00:21] Maya: Awesome. Ethan from Redwood is our systems engineer, he'll go deep on sizing and benchmarks. Ethan?
[00:00:26] Ethan: Hi all, thanks. quick agenda — understand your workloads, isolation needs, burst patterns, then go through how Redwood Dedicated handles reserved GPU pools, autoscale, and network/security options.
[00:00:36] Priya: Sounds good. high level: we run a mix of synchronous inference for customer-facing analytics (p95 ~80-120ms target) and heavy batch jobs at end of day — those spike CPU/GPU usage, so we want reserved capacity for consistent latency but ability to burst. also strict data controls, we need audit logs and KMS for keys.
[00:00:55] Ethan: got it. when you say burst, what's the qps hit during end-of-day? and how long are the spikes?
[00:01:02] Daniel: spikes about 10x baseline for 20–40 minutes, and smaller hourly bursts during market open/close. baseline is ~50 requests/s, bursts up to ~500 requests/s.
[00:01:11] Maya: That's helpful — what models are you serving and sequence lengths?
[00:01:15] Priya: We use a trimmed LLM for summarization and a custom reranker. seq lengths about 512 tokens for most requests, some long batch runs to 2k tokens for nightly.
[00:01:25] Ethan: cool, that helps with GPU selection. for dedicated we recommend reserved pools sized to baseline with a burst policy. Redwood Dedicated supports guaranteed reserved GPUs plus burst lanes that draw from shared burst capacity — we can do predictable autoscaling with hard caps to protect isolation.
[00:01:40] Tom: can you explain the isolation model? we need tenant isolation and basically no noisy neighbor impact for critical paths.
[00:01:45] Ethan: yes — Dedicated gives you a reserved cluster (dedicated GPU nodes) logically isolated from other tenants. network isolation via VPC peering or private link, and we support customer-managed KMS for model encryption. burst lanes may live on shared infra but we can configure fallbacks so critical routes always stay on reserved nodes; non-critical batch can be allowed to burst.
[00:02:07] Priya: ah ok so we can pin low-latency endpoints to reserved GPUs and allow batch to use burst — what about warm KV cache behavior? we rely on KV cache for chat-like flows and need high hit rate.
[00:02:19] Ethan: we do prefix/KV cache on the dedicated nodes; caching is preserved during autoscale up to the node's cache. when bursting to shared GPUs the cache cold-starts, so you typically want hot routes pinned. there's also a hybrid approach — keep small reserved pool for hot paths and autoscale batch.
[00:02:36] Daniel: what about burst capacity guarantees? do you throttle or queue?
[00:02:40] Maya: to add, pricing wise we usually tier based on reserved commit and a smaller usage for burst minutes. we'll include a sample committed pricing table in the follow-up.
[00:02:48] Ethan: on the runtime side we support graceful degradation — if burst capacity is exhausted requests can be queued with a short timeout, fall back to lighter quantized model, or reroute to hosted variants. You can configure fallback policies per route.
[00:03:04] Tom: latency constraints — our p95 SLA is 120ms; can you meet that under baseline and bursts?
[00:03:11] Ethan: Under reserved capacity yes, for the pinned endpoints we optimize kernels, batching, and KV cache. For bursts that hit shared infra depends — if you allow batch to burst there may be higher tail latency. We can run a benchmark to validate with your payloads.
[00:03:24] Priya: we care about model compatibility — we do quantized 4-bit for cost. does Redwood support custom quantization?
[00:03:30] Ethan: support for quantized variants is in the runtime, we can onboard your quantized model and test perf. We also recommend model selection — some architectures work better with our kernel compilation.
[00:03:40] Liam: security — SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and key management. also need to know where logs live and retention.
[00:03:46] Sophie: we have SOC 2 and audit logs; for Dedicated we can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder. logs retention configurable per contract. KMS integration supports customer-managed keys so we never hold plaintext keys.
[00:03:59] Liam: do you support HSM?
[00:04:01] Maya: yes — we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers — we'll include supported KMS vendors in the security doc.
[00:04:07] Daniel: network-wise, we need to peer into our VPC and lock down IPs. also curious about private deployment vs hosted dedicated — what's the tradeoff operationally?
[00:04:16] Ethan: Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you more control and no shared control plane; dedicated is hosted but gives logical isolation and reserved GPUs. Private is heavier setup and longer lead time but is ideal for strict compliance. Dedicated is faster to spin up and still meets many enterprise needs.
[00:04:32] Priya: what's typical lead time for dedicated pools?
[00:04:35] Maya: depends on size—small pools (couple of GPUs) we can provision in days, larger reserved clusters take a few weeks to ensure capacity. For pilots we often do a 1-week dedicated pilot on a smaller pool.
[00:04:46] Tom: billing and commitments — can you do monthly or do we need annual?
[00:04:50] Maya: both options; committed monthly or annual terms with discounts for longer-term. also burst usage billed at usage rates, we can show an example P&L.
[00:04:58] Daniel: curious about SLOs — what uptime/latency SLAs do you offer?
[00:05:02] Sophie: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA doc. For mission critical paths we recommend geographic redundancy.
[00:05:11] Priya: for the benchmark—what do you need from us?
[00:05:14] Ethan: we'll need a sample of request traces, payloads, p95 targets, a subset of models or a container with your model if possible, and a short test script. we'll run baseline and burst scenarios and produce token-level latency/cost breakdowns.
[00:05:28] Priya: we can share traces and a reranker container, yes.
[00:05:31] Liam: any compliance docs ahead of the security call?
[00:05:33] Sophie: yes — we'll send SOC 2, ISO summary, network diagrams, and the dedicated/private datasheet.
[00:05:40] Tom: decision timeline — we aim to pick vendor within 6 weeks, pilot in 2–3 weeks.
[00:05:46] Maya: great — our recommended next step is to send pricing + contract template, security docs, and schedule the SE-led benchmark. does that align?
[00:05:55] Daniel: yes that works.
[00:05:57] Priya: could we include a short runbook on failover? e.g., how to fallback to hosted endpoints if dedicated has issues.
[00:06:03] Ethan: yes — we have automatic fallback routing with canary and A/B rollouts; we'll include examples of routing policies and runbook snippets.
[00:06:10] Tom: ok thanks, I'll drop after 25 minutes but appreciate the clarity.
[00:06:13] Maya: thanks Tom.
[00:06:15] Daniel: a few quick clarifying q's — are there hard isolation certifications for dedicated to guarantee no cross-tenant access?
[00:06:22] Sophie: we provide attestations and network isolation; for absolute guarantees customers choose Private on-prem. but Dedicated includes logical isolation and hardened access controls.
[00:06:33] Priya: for atlas of metrics — can we get token-level cost estimates by route?
[00:06:38] Ethan: yes — Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. we'll include sample screenshots.
[00:06:45] Daniel: ok let's recap next steps.
[00:06:48] Maya: recap — Maya to send pricing & contract, Ethan to run benchmark plan and schedule pilot, Priya to share traces and model container, Liam to share network allowlist, Sophie to send security docs.
[00:06:58] Tom: perfect.
[00:07:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the attachments and a Doodle for the pilot window.

End of transcript.
